TextBlock.Text: THEATRE Banda Sea, between Tanimbar and Kai
DATE 3 November 2028 · 0540 local
SIDE Royal Australian Navy
WINDOW 110 min, closes at 165
Peykaap III-class. Photo: Fars Media Corporation · CC BY 4.0 · cropped
"Air superiority is not guaranteed. It must be earned every day."
- Gen. Kenneth S. Wilsbach, Chief of Staff, US Air Force, 2025

BANDA SEA APPROACHES, 0540, between the Tanimbar and Kai groups. A Meridian convoy left the Arafura last night with its transponders off and is going north for the Banda Sea and Biak: two cargo ships, the armed merchant MV Meridian Vigilant with a 57 mm gun, two fast attack craft ahead and a trawler astern. A sixth hull is radiating like a frigate and is almost certainly not one: the same trick Meridian Assurance played on the eighteenth of October.

Weapons Free has held for a day. The cargo ships are lawful targets under the new rules; the Indonesian fishing boats and the tanker going south are not. Your detachment is south-west of the convoy, forty miles off, with the Seahawk if you embarked one.

Stop both cargo ships before they reach the Banda Sea entrance. The boats will come for you when they see you, the armed merchant will fight, and the trawler astern is the one that sank a fishing boat off Dobo last week with something that was not a gun.
Commodore Alex Mercer
COMMANDER'S INTENT

They have read yesterday the way we have: the rules changed and they are moving everything they can before we use them. Two cargo ships with the enclave's next month in them, an armed merchant riding shotgun, two boats out front, and something with a lot of radars on it that wants to be mistaken for a frigate. The cargo is the target. Find out which hull is which before you spend a missile, and leave the fishermen out of it.
• Stop both cargo ships before they reach the Banda Sea
• Sink the armed merchant Meridian Vigilant
• Classify the radar decoy
• Bring your lead ship out
• Harm no fishing boat or tanker

Your detachment, and its Seahawk if one is embarked. Opposing: two cargo ships, the armed merchant Meridian Vigilant, a radar decoy, two Peykaap fast attack craft and an armed trawler. Neutral: two Indonesian fishing boats and a southbound tanker.

The planned window is 110 minutes. At that minute Command signals that you are behind schedule and holds the line for about 55 minutes more; the operation is closed at 165 minutes and the main task will be recorded as failed.
RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
All designated neutral contacts are protected. A protected neutral loss cancels the operation. Identify before you shoot.
